assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is a foundational, minimal model of non-equilibrium interface growth and defines a broad universality class with exact solutions linking to random matrices (Tracy-Widom statistics). Experimental realisation in liquid-crystal turbulence is a rare case of precise confirmation of a non-equilibrium scaling law. Originality, conceptual clarity and reach across stochastic dynamics are high.
assessment.attribution: Kardar and Zhang are the theoretical originators of the supplied credit; Takeuchi provided the decisive quantitative experimental confirmation. The 1986 paper also had Giorgio Parisi, who is not among the credited names, and the many mathematical-physics contributors to exact solutions are not credited, so any trio leaves a fair-allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Theory dates from 1986 and the experimental confirmation from 2010-2012, with extensive subsequent verification across systems; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be framed around the theory-experiment pair or require recognising the exact-solution work that is not credited
Parisi's co-authorship and prior prize complicate attribution
Experimental universality is established mainly in a few systems

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture gives a unifying, concrete statistical-mechanical framework for the onset of rigidity in disordered matter (foams, grains, emulsions, glasses), with critical scaling, anomalous vibrational modes and a clear connection to the glass problem. It is original and conceptually clean, and has had strong lasting impact in soft matter.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel's 1998 paper and subsequent work are widely identified as the origin, and the two-person credit is clean. Contributions from O'Hern, Silbert, Wyart, Torquato and others on the critical nature of the transition are not credited and may be relevant.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of numerical and experimental work support the framework, though how far it explains the glass transition and real thermal systems is still debated; recognition is reasonable but the scope is not fully settled.
uncertainties: Extent to which jamming critical behaviour applies to real, finite-temperature glasses
Credit for the critical-scaling follow-up work by others
Experimental confirmation is more indirect than for a single decisive measurement

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, a new tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. Originality and impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental discovery together with Cao and others. The credited trio is a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration, though Cao's role as the lead experimentalist is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Discovery is recent (2018) but heavily reproduced by independent groups; the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is not settled, which argues for some patience.
uncertainties: Superconducting mechanism remains unresolved
Credit for the student leading the experimental work is not among the credited names
Early-career timing relative to other topics

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a new classification of band structures, with robust edge and surface states, and reshaped condensed-matter theory and materials research. Conceptual originality and lasting impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 quantum spin Hall state; Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe wells following Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore, Hasan and others are not all in the supplied credit, so the trio is defensible but leaves a hard allocation among several contributors.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in several materials through independent experiments over about 15 years; the idea is mature and well tested, and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Competing claims between 2D and 3D topological insulator contributors
Whether Molenkamp or another experimentalist best represents the confirmation
Overlap with the topological-phase recognition in the 2016 prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provides the architecture for coupling and reading out superconducting qubits and is the operating basis of leading quantum processors. It is original, clear and has large impact on quantum technology and fundamental light-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the 2004 proposal, and Wallraff, Schoelkopf and collaborators demonstrated strong coupling. Girvin is excluded under a three-person cap, and the superconducting-qubit prize in 2025 may overlap with this recognition.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent confirmation across laboratories; very mature, though recent recognition of macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits may reduce room.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recent prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits
Three-name limit excludes Girvin, a key theorist
Relative claim of the theory proposal versus the experiments

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise controllable Hubbard models, the Mott-superfluid transition and quantum simulation of many-body physics. This is a mature, high-impact line that connects strongly to statistical physics and has become a standard tool.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch proposed the Hubbard-model realisation; Greiner, Bloch and Hansch's group observed the Mott transition, and Esslinger demonstrated fermionic Mott insulators. Choosing three among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger and Zoller leaves a clear unresolved allocation.
assessment.maturity: Core results are from 1998-2002 and have been reproduced widely; quantum gas microscopy and simulation are mature, with long-standing recognition potential.
uncertainties: Four plausible credited people for a three-name cap
Overlap with earlier BEC and cold-atom prizes
Whether simulation results have yet produced decisive new physics

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC confirmed the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking and completed the Standard Model's particle content. Its significance is exceptional, with extensive subsequent measurement of couplings.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theory. The experimental credit is split among very large collaborations, and the three listed names are founding spokespersons or leaders rather than a clean individual-discovery set, which makes attribution difficult for a prize that cannot go to collaborations.
assessment.maturity: Discovery in 2012 is very strongly confirmed by independent ATLAS and CMS results and by Run 2 and 3 coupling measurements; recognition is mature, but attribution is the obstacle.
uncertainties: Fair attribution to leaders of thousands-strong collaborations
Whether named spokespersons embody the decisive contributions
The 2013 prize already acknowledged the discovery in part

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gives an exact treatment of local correlations in infinite dimensions and enables quantitative calculations for correlated materials, a statistical-physics-style mean-field idea with wide applicability.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar developed the mapping to an impurity model and Vollhardt with Metzner introduced the infinite-dimension limit; Metzner is not in the supplied credit, which leaves a significant attribution gap.
assessment.maturity: More than 30 years of use and extensions, with strong qualitative success, though accuracy for finite-dimensional real materials has limits; recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Metzner's decisive 1989 contribution is not in the credited names
Quantitative reliability for real materials remains debated
Relation to other numerical methods for strongly correlated systems
